relevance_note: Case report of one child with SSADH deficiency and a homozygous ALDH5A1 variant ('Sanger sequencing of ALDH5A1 revealed a homozygous variant'), with heterozygous parents and sibling and a literature table of two previously reported probands with the same genotype.
method_note: Rows built with a Python script from my own reading; every value hand-entered and every span checked verbatim by script. Table 1 has patients as columns: column 1 header 'Proband in our report' (= the case-report patient, labelled 'patient'), column 2 'Proband from Pakistan origin[1]', column 3 'Proband from Palestinian–Lebanese origin[1]'; columns 2 and 3 are previously reported probands (role-word headers, so labelled 'Table 1 column 2/3') with source '[1]'. Relatives: 'Her parents were heterozygous for the same variant' and Figure 2 legend 'Parents and the unaffected sibling are heterozygous'. The paper separately names 'her mother' (paralytic poliomyelitis), so one parent is labelled 'mother of patient' and the other, whose sex is never stated, 'parent of patient'; the sibling's sex and birth order are not stated. 'Age at presentation' in Table 1 was recorded as age at onset for all three probands; the case patient's age at diagnosis and age at last follow-up are not given as numbers (follow-up at 6 months and 2 years after diagnosis). Variant for relatives taken from 'the same variant'; for Table 1 columns 2-3 from the table title 'previously reported patients with the same genotype' (zygosity left not reported because it is not printed for them). The Discussion says the same variant was reported elsewhere under other nomenclature (c.1343 + 1delG and c.1343 + 3A>T) in 'at least three additional families'; these are not attributed to identifiable people, so no rows. Patient inheritance left 'not reported' because the enum has no biparental value (both parents heterozygous; statement in parental_testing_statement). Variant type 'splice' from 'change in the consensus splice donor site'. In silico predictions and ClinVar accession are not functional evidence. Table 1 'Yes'/'No' cells treated as explicit present/absent statements; 'No data' as not reported. 'Normal' cells (EEG, reflexes) recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27). Column 2 'Normal tone at presentation Hypotonia at follow-up' recorded as hypotonia observed (temporal, not contradictory). 'Extrapyramidal symptoms: No' was not used to exclude the narrower checklist items dystonia, exertional dyskinesia or hemiballismus for column 3. Hemiparesis counted as a gross motor deficit for the checklist. Developmental delay not recorded as intellectual disability; 'stranger anxiety' (a premorbid milestone) not recorded as anxiety. No contradictions found between text and Table 1 for the case patient. No stacked cells.
